First release of dropbear86, an SSH-2 client for [ELKS](https://github.com/ghaerr/elks) on 8086/8088 PCs, based on [Dropbear](https://github.com/mkj/dropbear).

## Read this first

This is experimental. ELKS has no `/dev/urandom`, so keys are generated from weak entropy sources. A seed saved in `/etc/dropbear.seed` improves this with every connection, but the first connection after installing is weak. Don't use it to reach anything you need to keep private.

## What works

- Full SSH-2 login with password authentication and an interactive session.
- Algorithms: `curve25519-sha256` key exchange, `ssh-ed25519` host keys, `chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com`. The server has to offer these; a stock OpenSSH server does.
- Tested on a Compaq Portable Plus (Intel 8088 @ 4.77 MHz) running ELKS master from 2026-09-30 with picoMEM's NE2000 emulation, against OpenSSH 10.0p2 with its default configuration.

## Performance

On a 4.77 MHz 8088, it takes about 3 minutes from running `ssh` to the password prompt, down from about 35 minutes before this release's optimizations: hand-written 8086 assembly for the Curve25519 field arithmetic, a faster Ed25519 signature check, no wasted key generation, and a workaround for an ELKS networking slowdown. About 55 s of the 3 minutes is ELKS loading the binary. The [README](https://github.com/sammothxc/dropbear86#performance) and [PERF.md](https://github.com/sammothxc/dropbear86/blob/v0.1.0/PERF.md) have the details.

## Install

1. Download `ssh` and copy it to `/bin/ssh` on your ELKS system. With ELKS's `ftp` client, run `binary` (or `type i`) before `get`; ASCII mode silently corrupts the binary.
2. Run `chmod 755 /bin/ssh`.
3. Check it with `md5sum /bin/ssh` against `MD5SUMS`. ELKS has no `sha256sum`; `SHA256SUMS` is there for checking the download on other systems.
4. Connect with `ssh -y user@host`. `-y` accepts the server's host key without a known-hosts prompt.

## Requirements

- An 8088 or better running a recent ELKS with working networking. picoMEM's NE2000 emulation needs ELKS master from 2026-09-30 or later.
- About 46 KB of ELKS's 64 KB per-process data segment.
- An SSH server offering the algorithms above. OpenSSH's default 2-minute `LoginGraceTime` works for password login: the prompt appears about 90 s after connecting, leaving roughly 30 s to type the password.

## Known limitations

- Weak entropy, as above.
- Public-key login is compiled in, but signing is slow enough to exceed OpenSSH's default `LoginGraceTime`, and it hasn't been tested with a key stored on ELKS.
- Starting `ssh` takes about 55 s on an 8088, even for `ssh -V`, because of how ELKS loads programs.
